output.proposal: HB No. 10699 seeks to increase the total permanent physical disability, killed-in-action and retirement benefits of members of the Philippine National Police (PNP) by amending Sections 73 and 75 of RA No. 6975, as amended by RA No. 8551. It does not create a new body.
output.alignment: As the measure amends the benefit provisions of an existing agency's charter rather than creating a new body, the review should focus on the fiscal impact of the enhanced disability, killed-in-action and retirement pensions on the PNP's personnel services and pension obligations, and on consistency with other pending proposals on uniformed personnel pension reform; organizational streamlining under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231) is of limited relevance since no office is created or restructured. The FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework priority area tagged for the measure (Implementation of full devolution to LGUs) does not appear to correspond to its subject matter, and no LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda item is identified for it.
legislative_history: HB No. 10699 was filed on August 11, 2026 by Representative Mauricio G. Domogan in the 20th Congress; its status is filed, with later stages not yet recorded.

HB No. 2178 (20th Congress, filed July 21, 2025, pending in the Committee) and HB No. 5505 (19th Congress, filed October 10, 2022, pending in the Committee) carry titles on adjusting the total permanent physical disability benefit under Section 73 of RA No. 6975; title match only, text not reviewed.
HB No. 9418 (20th Congress) similarly seeks to strengthen PNP disability and survivorship benefits by amending RA No. 6975, as amended by RA No. 8551.
HB No. 7945 (19th Congress) and HB No. 5155 (18th Congress), both pending in the Committee, also sought to amend Section 73 of RA No. 6975 based on their titles.
No Senate counterpart, substitute bill or committee report was identified.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 10699 seeks to enhance the disability, killed-in-action and retirement benefits of uniformed members of the Philippine National Police by amending Sections 73 and 75 of RA No. 6975, as amended by RA No. 8551. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 1 (Short Title) provides that the measure shall be known as the New Retirement Pension, Total Permanent Physical Disability and Killed in Action Benefit for Members of the Philippine National Police.
b. Section 2 (Amendment of Section 73 of RA No. 6975) provides that an officer or non-officer certified as permanently and totally disabled in the line of duty shall receive one year's salary and a lifetime pension of 90 percent of the most updated salary of the last salary grade, with the pension passing to the surviving spouse or dependent children for the balance of a five-year guaranteed period if the member dies within five years of retirement, and that the legal beneficiaries of personnel killed in action shall receive a lifetime pension at the same 90 percent rate regardless of years in active duty.
c. Section 3 (Amendment of Section 75 of RA No. 6975) provides that monthly retirement pay shall be 50 percent of monthly base and longevity pay for 20 years of active duty, increasing by 2.5 percent for every year beyond 20 years up to 90 percent for 36 years and over, with an option to receive the first three years in advance as a lump sum payable within six months, and with retirement pay adjusted to the prevailing base pay scale of active police personnel.
d. Section 4 (Appropriations) provides that initial funding shall be charged against the current appropriations of the PNP, and thereafter included in the succeeding General Appropriations Act.
e. Section 5 (Implementing Rules and Regulations) provides that the DILG, NAPOLCOM, DBM and PNP shall promulgate the implementing rules within 90 days from effectivity.
f. Section 7 (Repealing Clause) provides for the repeal of Sections 73 and 75 of RA No. 6975, as amended by RA No. 8551, and of inconsistent laws and issuances.
g. Section 8 (Effectivity) provides that the Act shall take effect 15 days after publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 10699 may be considered alongside HB No. 9418 and HB No. 2178 in the 20th Congress, which likewise address PNP disability and survivorship benefits under Section 73 of RA No. 6975, and HB No. 9723, which proposes a new separation, retirement and pension system for military and uniformed personnel. The measure does not correspond to a specific FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework priority area or LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda item. The review should assess the fiscal implications of raising the disability and killed-in-action pension to 90 percent of the most updated salary and of indexing retirement pay to the prevailing base pay scale under Section 2 (Amendment of Section 73 of RA No. 6975) and Section 3 (Amendment of Section 75 of RA No. 6975), the sufficiency of charging initial costs to current PNP appropriations under Section 4 (Appropriations), and consistency with broader uniformed personnel pension reform proposals.
